findings.claim: The narrowed R-012/R-013 requirement sentence restricts the roadmap-maker obligation to 'the agent-compute-time field' (singular), but its own paired scenario and the shipped R013 assertion enforce a broader five-field prohibition spanning all three independently tracked units, so requirement text and enforced contract disagree in scope.
proof_refs: openspec/changes/actuals-calendar-checkpoint-instrumentation/specs/actuals-instrumentation/spec.md:93 states "MUST NOT source tracking-line figures from the agent-compute-time field", while line 104 of the same file scans for five structured field names: total_wall_clock_hours, checkpoint_count, implementation_hours, review_gate_hours, post_review_fix_hours.

engine/skills/actuals_instrumentation_contract_test.go:162-165 forbids that identical five-name list, so the enforced contract is the five-field one, not the single-field one the requirement sentence states.

openspec/changes/actuals-calendar-checkpoint-instrumentation/specs/actuals-instrumentation/spec.md:63 defines the compute-time baseline as built only from implementation_hours, review_gate_hours, and post_review_fix_hours, so only three of the five forbidden names are compute-time fields; total_wall_clock_hours and checkpoint_count are the two other independently tracked units.

Failure scenario: non-blocking today, because the roadmap-maker skill document is untouched by this candidate and contains none of the five names. Latent risk: a future edit adding a legitimate ownership-attributing prose mention of checkpoint_count or total_wall_clock_hours to that document, which the paired scenario's own 'prose correctly attributing ownership' clause treats as valid, would still trip the literal five-name prohibition and fail the build.

findings.claim: Both new RED groups pin their markers with a whole-file strings.Contains and no anchor to the section the marker is supposed to live in, and R001_R002_three_units_never_blended never asserts its own scenario's 'all three units are named' clause, only the requirement tag and the never-blended phrase.
proof_refs: engine/skills/actuals_instrumentation_contract_test.go:137-144 ranges over the literal slice {"R-001/R-002", "never summed or averaged into one figure"} and calls strings.Contains against the whole file contents with no section scoping; lines 149-152 do the same for the single R-012 marker "elapsed-calendar-time, and checkpoint count under separate labels, never blended".

Neither group asserts the three unit-name substrings agent-compute-time, elapsed-calendar-time, and human-confirmation-checkpoint-count that openspec/changes/actuals-calendar-checkpoint-instrumentation/specs/actuals-instrumentation/spec.md:17 requires to be present.

Failure scenario: non-blocking today, because each pinned marker is a unique single-occurrence string in the time-estimation skill document. Latent risk: because the checks are file-scoped rather than section-scoped, relocating the pinned bytes into an unrelated section would still pass; separately, an edit that dropped the explicit three-unit naming from the Hard Rules bullet while leaving the requirement tag and the never-blended phrase intact elsewhere in the file would still pass R001_R002_three_units_never_blended even though the paired scenario at line 17 of the spec would then be violated.

findings.claim: The new R-013 scenario's THEN clause asserts that the roadmap-maker document's 'only' actuals-related mention is ownership-attributing prose; no shipped assertion checks that exclusivity clause, and the word 'only' is literally inaccurate against the current document, though every mention there is substantively consistent with the ownership claim.
proof_refs: openspec/changes/actuals-calendar-checkpoint-instrumentation/specs/actuals-instrumentation/spec.md:105 reads "THEN none appear as a tracking-line data source, and its only actuals-related mention is prose correctly attributing ownership of those fields to inception-pipeline closure-feedback".

A case-insensitive search for the word actuals in the roadmap-maker skill document matches nine distinct lines, not one; every match is consistent with the ownership attribution, so the clause is substantively right but its quantifier 'only' is wrong.
engine/skills/actuals_instrumentation_contract_test.go:155-170 asserts only the five-name prohibition and nothing about exclusivity, so this clause is unasserted.

Failure scenario: not a wrong outcome. No shipped assertion claims to verify the exclusivity clause, so there is no false pass and no false failure tied to it; the imprecision is confined to the scenario's own prose.
